cases.name: legacy-bound-perpetual
cases.description: Legacy format bound to the expected machine, without expiration.

cases.name: legacy-unbound-dated
cases.description: Empty hardware ID: valid on any machine until 00:00 UTC on 2027-06-11.

cases.name: legacy-expires-at-check-date
cases.description: Expires at 00:00 UTC on the check date, so it is already expired at 12:00 UTC that day.

cases.name: legacy-expires-next-day
cases.description: Expires at 00:00 UTC on the day after the check date, so it is still current.

cases.name: format2-user-defined
cases.description: Format 2 with signed UserDefined text.

cases.name: format2-separator-and-unicode
cases.description: Format 2 allows the legacy separator and any Unicode text in its fields.

cases.name: bound-to-another-machine
cases.description: Authentic, but bound to a different hardware ID.

cases.name: issued-for-another-product
cases.description: Authentic, but issued for another product with the same key.

cases.name: tampered-registration-name
cases.description: The customer name was changed after signing.

cases.name: tampered-expiration
cases.description: An expired license whose date was moved forward after signing.

cases.name: legacy-separator-in-field
cases.description: A legacy-format field containing the separator; rejected before the signature is checked.

cases.name: unsupported-format-version
cases.description: A format version this verifier does not know.

cases.name: unsigned-property-at-nesting-limit
cases.description: An unsigned property that nests the JSON to its 8-level limit; verifiers ignore it.

cases.name: nesting-beyond-limit
cases.description: The same unsigned property nested one level beyond the 8-level limit.

cases.name: byte-order-mark
cases.description: The license JSON starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, which JSON does not allow.

cases.name: signature-with-spaces
cases.description: Spaces inserted into the Base64 signature; the license and its revocation identifier are unchanged.

cases.name: signature-with-no-break-space
cases.description: Only spaces, tabs, carriage returns and line feeds are ignored inside the Signature text; a no-break space is malformed.

cases.name: signature-not-base64
cases.description: A Signature text that is not standard Base64 is malformed, not a signature mismatch.

cases.name: missing-expiration-date
cases.description: The ExpirationDate property is absent, which reads as null.

cases.name: duplicate-property
cases.description: The root object repeats a property name.

cases.name: non-standard-constant
cases.description: An unsigned property holds NaN, which JSON does not allow.

cases.name: trailing-comma
cases.description: The root object ends with a comma.

cases.name: comment
cases.description: The JSON contains a comment.

cases.name: text-after-object
cases.description: Text follows the root object.

cases.name: lone-surrogate
cases.description: A signed field contains an unpaired surrogate escape.

cases.name: unpaired-surrogate-in-property-name
cases.description: An unpaired surrogate escape in a property name of the root object is malformed, even in an unknown property.

cases.name: unsigned-property-with-unpaired-surrogate
cases.description: The value of an unknown property is not read: an unpaired surrogate escape in it leaves the license authentic.

cases.name: blank-unicode-name
cases.description: The registration name is only an em space, which is blank.

cases.name: file-separator-name
cases.description: The registration name is U+001C, which .NET does not treat as whitespace: the name is not blank, so the changed claim fails the signature.

cases.name: app-id-too-long
cases.description: The product identifier exceeds 128 UTF-16 code units.

cases.name: app-id-at-utf-8-byte-limit
cases.description: An AppId of 128 UTF-16 code units and 255 UTF-8 bytes is within the limits, so the changed claim fails only the signature.

cases.name: app-id-beyond-utf-8-byte-limit
cases.description: An AppId of 128 UTF-16 code units and 256 UTF-8 bytes exceeds the byte limit.

cases.name: registration-name-at-utf-16-limit
cases.description: A RegistrationName of 512 emoji is 1,024 UTF-16 code units, within the limit, so the changed claim fails only the signature.

cases.name: registration-name-beyond-utf-16-limit
cases.description: One more character makes 1,025 UTF-16 code units: lengths count code units, not characters or bytes.

cases.name: fractional-format-version
cases.description: FormatVersion is written with a fraction.

cases.name: boolean-format-version
cases.description: FormatVersion is a boolean.

cases.name: numeric-expiration-date
cases.description: ExpirationDate is a number instead of a date text.

cases.name: format2-without-user-defined
cases.description: Format 2 with empty custom text.

cases.name: format2-downgraded
cases.description: The format 2 version was removed, leaving custom text in a legacy license.

cases.name: format2-tampered-user-defined
cases.description: The custom text was changed after signing.

cases.name: legacy-empty-user-defined
cases.description: An empty UserDefined reads as null, so a legacy license that carries it is still authentic and has no custom data.

cases.name: whitespace-user-defined-without-format-2
cases.description: A UserDefined of one space is not empty, so it requires FormatVersion 2.

cases.name: format2-whitespace-user-defined
cases.description: Format 2 with a UserDefined of one space is well formed; the changed custom text fails only the signature.

cases.name: unsupported-format-before-date
cases.description: An unknown format version is reported before an invalid date is read.

cases.name: unsupported-format-after-unpaired-surrogate
cases.description: Claim texts are read before FormatVersion: an unpaired surrogate in a name is malformed even with an unknown version.

cases.name: unsupported-format-before-text-limit
cases.description: FormatVersion is read before the text limits: an unknown version with an AppId over 128 code units is an unsupported format.

cases.name: hardware-not-checked
cases.description: The application deliberately skips the hardware check of a bound license.

cases.name: unbound-without-hardware-check
cases.description: An unbound license inspected without an expected hardware ID is valid, but a verify function returns no license without one.

cases.name: blank-expected-product
cases.description: The application passes a blank product identifier.

cases.name: public-key-with-vertical-tab-inside
cases.description: Only spaces, tabs, carriage returns and line feeds may appear inside the PEM body; a vertical tab is rejected there.

cases.name: public-key-with-unicode-whitespace-around
cases.description: Any whitespace of the contract may surround the PEM block, such as U+0085, a no-break space or U+2028.

cases.name: public-key-too-small
cases.description: A 1024-bit RSA public key.

cases.name: not-a-license
cases.description: Text that is not Base64-encoded license JSON.

expirationTexts.description: Each text replaces the ExpirationDate value of the source license. Only the calendar date is signed, so an accepted text gives the source's published result and a rejected one is malformed. At the boundary, every accepted text is current at currentAt and expired at expiredAt: no time or offset moves the cutoff.

hardwareIdExamples.description: The hardware ID that the integration guide derives: HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with the UTF-8 product ID over the UTF-8 machine identifier without the spaces, tabs, carriage returns and line feeds at its ends, as 64 uppercase hexadecimal characters. Here the identifier is a Linux machine-id with its final line break. It is a recommendation for applications, not part of the license contract.
The same derivation keeps every other character at the ends, here a no-break space and a byte order mark, which the trim functions of some languages remove.
